title: Centre lathe — main parts
alt: Side-view line diagram of a centre lathe with lettered callouts A to Q

A.function: Houses the main spindle, speed gear box and change gears; carries the live centre

B.function: Grips and rotates the workpiece; attached to the headstock spindle

C.function: Main supporting structure on which headstock, tailstock and carriage are mounted

D.function: Supports the free end of long work; holds drills and reamers

E.function: Non-rotating centre in the tailstock that supports the work

F.function: Sliding spindle of the tailstock that carries the dead centre or a drill

G.function: Moves the tailstock quill in and out

H.function: H-shaped part of the carriage that slides along the bed ways

I.function: Moves the tool at right angles to the lathe axis; sets depth of cut

J.function: Swivelling top slide used for short tapers and angular cuts

K.function: Holds the cutting tool rigidly on top of the compound rest

L.function: Front of the carriage; contains the carriage handwheel, half-nut and feed levers

M.function: Long threaded shaft used only for thread cutting

N.function: Plain shaft that drives the carriage for turning and facing feeds

O.function: Supports the whole machine on the floor

P.function: Gives different feeds and thread pitches; drives the feed rod and lead screw

Q.function: Collects chips and coolant falling from the work

title: Lathe operations
alt: Ten small sketches of lathe operations, each marked with a letter A to J; orange arrows show feed direction

A.function: Flat end surface; tool fed perpendicular to the axis; reduces length

B.function: Diameter reduced along the length; tool fed parallel to the axis

C.function: Diameter reduced over part of the length, leaving a shoulder

D.function: Uniform change of diameter along the length; tool fed at the half-taper angle

E.function: Narrow groove cut by plunging a grooving tool radially

F.function: Tool plunged radially until the finished job is cut off

G.function: Bevels the sharp end edge (e.g. 45°) to remove burrs

H.function: Conical centre hole drilled from the tailstock so the work can be supported on a centre

I.function: Helical groove cut by a single-point tool fed one pitch per revolution

J.function: Pattern pressed (embossed) on the surface by knurling rollers

title: Universal dividing (indexing) head — schematic
alt: Schematic of a dividing head showing index plate, crank, worm and worm wheel driving the work spindle, with lettered callouts

A.function: Plate with circles of equally spaced holes used to count crank movement

B.function: Handle turned to rotate the worm; 40 turns = one turn of the work

C.function: Engages a hole of the selected circle to lock the crank

D.function: Set to span the required number of holes so they need not be counted each time

E.function: Driven by the crank; turns the worm wheel one tooth per revolution

F.function: Fixed to the work spindle; gives the 40 : 1 reduction

G.function: Carries the gear blank and rotates it by the indexed amount

H.function: Supports the outer end of the mandrel

title: Spur gear tooth nomenclature
alt: Enlarged view of five spur-gear teeth with outside, pitch and root circles and lettered terms

A.function: Radial height of the tooth above the pitch circle = 1/DP

B.function: Radial depth of the tooth below the pitch circle = 1.157/DP

C.function: Imaginary circle on which mating gears roll; diameter = N/DP

D.function: Circle through the tooth tips; diameter OD = (N + 2)/DP

E.function: Circle through the bottoms of the tooth spaces

F.function: Distance between corresponding points of adjacent teeth along the pitch circle = π/DP

G.function: Total depth of the tooth space = addendum + dedendum = 2.157/DP

H.function: Width of a tooth measured along the pitch circle = π/(2·DP)

title: Types of gears
alt: Seven simple line drawings of gear pairs, each marked with a letter

A.function: Parallel shafts; straight teeth parallel to the axis

B.function: Parallel shafts; teeth inclined to the axis, smoother running with axial thrust

C.function: Parallel shafts; opposite helices cancel the axial thrust

E.function: Non-intersecting shafts at 90°; large speed reduction

F.function: Converts rotary motion into straight-line motion

G.function: Teeth cut on the inside of a ring; meshes with a pinion on a parallel shaft
